matches.quote: Discuss non-unitary or time-reversal-breaking states and higher-order basis functions (e.g. k_x k_y k_z terms) that are allowed by symmetry.
STM, thermal conductivity and penetration-depth studies on UTe₂ indicate gaps of order ~0.2–0.4 meV... A factor of ~4 excess is far more naturally a symptom of fitting artifacts
The decisive symmetry assignment (B₂u vs B₃u) cannot be made from (001) data alone... where B₂u and B₃u become distinguishable.
non-hydrostaticity is invoked only ad hoc, to explain the double dips.
An anisotropic A_u state (strongly unequal Δ_i), as suggested by NMR and thermal conductivity, together with realistic Γ, may well reproduce a single broadened ZBCP.
The intrinsic (ZABS) origin of the ZBCP and, especially, the side dips is not established; non-ballistic/critical-current artifacts are not excluded.
Multicomponent states (e.g. B₂u + iB₃u, or mixtures with A_u) are not modelled... Discuss non-unitary or time-reversal-breaking states
UTe₂ has quasi-2D cylindrical Fermi sheets along c, with small v_z... The robustness of the main conclusions to this assumption ... is untested.
Side dips are a classic critical-current signature... The critical-current test is not performed at all under pressure, which is precisely where the dips appear.
Z ≈ 1.67 → ≈1.2; Γ ≈ 0.39 → ≈0.10 meV... The spectral 'evolution' may then partially reflect junction evolution rather than order-parameter evolution.
The superposition model (Eq. 2), with several channels each having its own (Δ_z, Δ_x, Z, Γ) plus weights w_i, has enough freedom to fit almost any multi-dip spectrum.
Multicomponent states (e.g. B₂u + iB₃u, or mixtures with A_u) are not modelled, even though a cited work (Wu et al., PRL 2025) argues SC3 may be multicomponent.
For the superposition model, limit the number of channels, justify w_i physically, and show that single-channel fits truly fail. Reconsider or justify the definition in Eq. 3.
The 1.4 GPa spectrum (Fig. 3d) is particularly telling: a broad, flat-topped peak bounded by sharp dips that move inward with temperature is precisely the critical-current pattern.
All pressure data come from a single sample and a single contact. There is no reproducibility under pressure on a second sample or contact.
No contact resistance R_N, no estimate of contact radius (Sharvin/Wexler) versus the electronic mean free path, and no I–V characteristics are given.
Table S1 lists Δ_z ≈ 1.15–1.18 meV and Δ_x(y) ≈ 0.60–0.72 meV... Either the Table S1 columns are swapped or the conclusions are reversed.
The ambient fits have 4 free parameters (Δ_z, Δ_x(y), Z, Γ)... Δ_z/Δ_x(y) is very likely strongly correlated with Z and Γ. Neither correlation matrices nor χ² landscapes are provided.
At 0.8 GPa, Γ = 0.10(1) meV and Z ≈ 1.20(1–2) are essentially constant across 0.5–2.1 K (Fig. S8).

notes: C12 is judged 'partly' because P6 notes the omitted kx ky kz higher-order basis functions and P22/P23/P25 challenge the B1u exclusion and idealized model, without explicitly stating that kx ky kz makes B1u sign-changing on (001). C16 is 'partly' because P14 and P24 challenge the ad-hoc pressure-inhomogeneity explanation of the 1.0-1.2 GPa double dips, though P14 attributes low-temperature solidification to Daphne 7373 rather than arguing inhomogeneity is small.
